note: Banco Atlántida only, as before: Banco Agrícola's, Banco Cuscatlán's, Davivienda's and BAC's card tariffs weren't reached in this pass. Banco Atlántida El Salvador's charges for its One credit card (updated 1 June 2026), read in full: a nominal interest rate of up to 51.95% a year, written at that top; no membership fee; a cash withdrawal of up to 5% of the sum, at least 5 dollars (nothing at the bank's own counters), written at 5%; a monthly late charge of 5% of the capital in arrears, at most 25 dollars, written as a share of the unpaid part; 15 dollars for a cheque payment returned; no moratory interest. Its amounts are before VAT, at a rate the document doesn't state, so none is added. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Banco Agrícola, the country's largest bank: its maximum rates, commissions and surcharges for credit cards (Banco Agrícola and Accelera), in force 1 to 31 October 2026, read in full (its right-hand columns were checked by eye against the table, since the text runs them together). Every personal card in the table (the Empresarial, Business, Mi Negocio, Lifemiles Pyme and Corporate Lifemiles are business cards): its nominal annual rate, a maximum ('hasta'), written as the rate; the Visa Platinum and Platinum Lifemiles each have two rows by credit limit (27.90% and 24.90%; 35.90% and 28.90%), written at the higher rate with the lower as the range's lowest and at the higher limit's membership (200 dollars; 125 and 100 at the lower limit), a fee charged in full; the main card's yearly membership (none where the table gives a dash); a cash withdrawal of 5% of the sum plus VAT (3.50% on the Mastercard Black), at a VAT rate the table doesn't state, so none is added; and 5.65 dollars a month until an overdraft is covered, written as the over-limit fee. The protection plan (a yearly insurance) isn't written; the late surcharge, 5% a year on the capital in arrears, is a rate on top and isn't written as a penalty rate. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated. Tried and not used: Banco Cuscatlán's and Banco Hipotecario's pages load their figures by script, Davivienda El Salvador's address answered with a near-empty page, Banco Promerica's and BAC Credomatic's El Salvador sites didn't answer, and the Superintendencia del Sistema Financiero's page on rates, commissions and surcharges gives no table to a plain request.
